title: Robots That Ask For Help: Uncertainty Alignment for Large Language Model Planners
authors: Allen Z. Ren, Anushri Dixit, Alexandra Bodrova, Sumeet Singh, Stephen Tu, et al.
problem: Told to put the bowl in the microwave, with a metal and a plastic bowl on the counter, an LLM planner may confidently pick one, and the metal one is unsafe.
idea: The LLM lists candidate next steps, then scores them as a multiple-choice question.
Conformal prediction keeps every option that clears a calibrated cut-off. One option left: act. More: ask.

figure.caption: Fig. 2, right panel: calibration sets the score threshold at 0.32; only option B (0.56) clears it: one option left.

takeaway: Score the candidate steps as a multiple-choice question and let conformal prediction set the cut-off: one option left means act, more means ask.
finding: The guarantee covers the plan, not the outcome
method: Candidate steps A to D come from a few-shot prompt; E, "an option not listed here", is added.
Calibration score: one minus the LLM's probability of the true option, on N = 400 labelled scenarios.

formula.reads: The set keeps every option the LLM scores at least $1-\hat{q}$.

measures: Plan success: the plan is correct, before the robot acts.
Help rate: the share of trials in which the robot asks.

certifies.event: the prediction set holds no correct option
certifies.guarantee: coverage, with probability 1 − δ over calibration
certifies.assumes: i.i.d. scenarios; the human answers correctly when asked
certifies.quote: In practice, we use a modest-sized calibration dataset (N = 400) and δ = 0.01

results.text: Kitchen, PaLM-2L, target 0.85: plan success 0.87, help rate 0.67.
Simple Set, at equal plan success 0.87: help rate 0.81.

limits: Execution is outside it: task success is 0.76 at the 0.85 target.
for_us: An act-or-ask gate can reuse the one-option rule as it is; to bound wrong grasps, the certified event must be the physical outcome, not the plan.
notes: Task success 0.76 is Table 2's Task Succ column (p.8). The paper puts low-level action success near 86% and names it as the cause of the gap between plan and task success (p.23). Accurate human help is assumed in the proof of Proposition 1 (p.5).
